topics: VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink tradeoffs
Region selection and data residency requirements (US-EAST-1, EU-WEST-1)
Egress constraints and corporate NAT/proxy considerations
Benchmarking plan: throughput, latency, token seq lengths
Success criteria: latency P95 < 150ms, 10k tokens/min throughput, data never leaves selected regions
transcript: 00:00:00 - Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see Jordan, Sana, Marcus, and we've got Priya from infra. We'll go through POC scoping for private networking and residency.
00:00:12 - Jordan Li: Yep thanks. Quick context: HealthScale processes PHI-ish telemetry, so data residency and egress are hard requirements. We're evaluating Redwood Private behind our VPC.
00:00:25 - Sana Rahman: Our ask is can we keep inference traffic inside our org's AWS accounts and ensure logs and model data never leave the chosen regions. Also cost on egress is a concern.

00:00:40 - Priya Nair: Right, two typical patterns: VPC peering between customer VPC and Redwood-managed VPC, or AWS PrivateLink endpoints. Peering is simpler for bi-directional connectivity, PrivateLink reduces route table exposure but has per-GB charges.

00:01:02 - Marcus D.: For us, corporate policy demands no cross-region egress without approval. We want to pin to us-east-1 or eu-west-1 depending on data type. Can Redwood support single-region deployment?

00:01:20 - Avery Chen: Yes, Redwood Private can be deployed per-region. We can pin the inference runtime and storage to your selected region and ensure control plane connectivity is private. There are subtle differences depending on the connectivity method.
00:01:35 - Jordan Li: What's the latency impact if we do PrivateLink vs peering? Our SLA target for interactive features is P95 under 150 milliseconds.

00:01:48 - Priya Nair: PrivateLink typically adds a small hop to the VPC endpoint but avoids NAT traversal; peering keeps direct routing. In practice with colocated infra, both can meet 150ms P95. We'll validate in the benchmark though — that's part of the POC.
00:02:10 - Sana Rahman: Egress costs — PrivateLink will incur VPC endpoint data processing fees. Peering avoids that but could expose cross-account connectivity questions for our security team.

00:02:25 - Avery Chen: We'll include a cost estimate for both in the doc. Also note that Private deployments can use your KMS for disk encryption and we support customer-managed keys so logs at rest can be under your KMS.
00:02:40 - Marcus D.: Ok, on telemetry retention: do you have controls to prevent model inputs from being persisted in any multi-tenant store? We need strict retention and audit logs.

00:02:52 - Priya Nair: Yes, retention is configurable. For POC we'll set logs to minimal retention and route audit logs to your CloudWatch or S3 bucket in the same account. There's a small plumbing effort to set up cross-account delivery.

00:03:08 - Jordan Li: Success criteria: besides residency, we want to prove performance — target throughput of 10k tokens/min sustained under peak, latency P95 < 150ms, and no data crossing regions. Anything else?

00:03:22 - Avery Chen: Also ease of ops: ability to rotate keys, RBAC integration with your IdP (we support SAML/SSO), and a defined rollback/fallback to hosted models if Dedicated capacity hits issues during POC.
00:03:36 - Sana Rahman: On the IdP, we need SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Is that part of the Private offering?
00:03:44 - Priya Nair: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in the customer control plane. We'll include an integration checklist.
00:03:55 - Jordan Li: Benchmarking: what's the plan? We need reproducible results we can show to infra and compliance.

00:04:03 - Priya Nair: We'll run a three-phase benchmark: 1) connectivity and cold-start latency with 1-4 concurrent requests, 2) throughput ramp up to target concurrency with 8k token sequences to stress KV cache, 3) steady-state run to measure cost and P95/P99 latencies. We'll provide the harness and test vectors.
00:04:25 - Marcus D.: For the test harness, can we run it from a bastion in our account to mirror production egress paths? We don't want tests going via public internet.
00:04:33 - Priya Nair: Absolutely — we'll provide an agent you can run inside your VPC. For PrivateLink we'll validate endpoint DNS and certs; for peering it's just route table and SG checks.
00:04:48 - Jordan Li: Any chance of transcribed errors: sorry — uh — I mean, any constraints around corporate proxy? We have strict outbound proxies so NAT egress is mandatory in some accounts.
00:04:58 - Sana Rahman: Yes some accounts do egress via proxy, that will affect connectivity model. Prefer peering in that case to avoid proxy bottlenecks.
00:05:10 - Avery Chen: Noted. We'll add a proxy/NAT checklist. Also we'll need your AWS account IDs and CIDR ranges to draft peering proposals. Marcus, you'll own that?
00:05:20 - Marcus D.: Yep I can provide those. Will also enumerate any approved egress destinations and ports; we typically only allow 443 to audited endpoints.

00:05:32 - Priya Nair: Good. Regarding data residency certification, we'll include the deployment manifest and attestation that storage and compute remain in- region. For audit we'll supply logs with region tags.
00:05:46 - Jordan Li: Timeline — what does Redwood recommend for a POC run from kickoff to benchmark report?

00:05:53 - Avery Chen: Typical timeline: week 0-1: network setup and connectivity validation; week 2: deployment and small-scale smoke tests; week 3: run benchmarks and iterate; week 4: review results and handoff. So about 3-4 weeks end-to-end.
00:06:10 - Sana Rahman: Works for us. We'll need the network workshop scheduled early so security can sign off on peering/PrivateLink decisions.
00:06:18 - Priya Nair: We'll propose two slots for the workshop in the next two business days. Also I'll attach the benchmark plan and sample scripts in the follow-up email.
00:06:30 - Jordan Li: Competitors — just so you're aware, we've looked at Anthropic's endpoint and an internal on-prem inference stack. The tie-breaker is residency and predictable unit cost.
00:06:42 - Avery Chen: Understood. We'll surface cost projections for peering vs PrivateLink and show latency/cost tradeoffs from our prior benchmarks.
00:06:52 - Marcus D.: Quick question — does Redwood require internet egress for control plane functions, or can the control plane be in a private VPC connected via VPN?

00:07:02 - Priya Nair: Control plane communications can be configured to use a private connection depending on the Private offering; we have options for VPN or direct interconnect for the control plane. We'll document requirements.

00:07:15 - Avery Chen: Great. Let's recap next steps: we'll share network diagram and security docs, Priya will send benchmark plan, Marcus/Sana to provide CIDRs and account IDs, and we'll schedule the network workshop. Anything missing?
00:07:30 - Jordan Li: No that's it. Thanks everyone — we'll look out for the docs and schedule.
00:07:36 - Avery Chen: Thanks all. Talk soon.
00:08:00 - [call ends]
